title: A song about painting, and red brick on the steps
summary: He recalls a song about a woman who paints her cheeks and how people once frowned on paint; Gerdy remembers scouring steps with red brick.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. So she didn't like that very much.

We used to use red brick. We had to wash the steps on a Saturday morning. In them days, when we was kids, you had to wash the front steps, you know. You always kept them nice and clean. And then after we washed them, we'd grind this brick up fine and throw it all over those steps. Well, some people did it to keep the bumps from sitting on these steps, you know. Dirty them up. But that was our job when we was kids. Every Saturday we had to go out and clean them and wash the back and wash the front steps. And we always had to do something. And if you were a real good kid, they'd give you a big nickel, you know.
